narr: Slow-moving thunderstorms resulted in flooding and flash flooding across portions of southern Herkimer County during the afternoon and early evening hours on May 6, 2025. Flooding was mostly concentrated within the villages of Ilion, Mohawk and Herkimer, where 2 to 3 inches of rain fell in a 1 to 2 hour period. While most of the flooding occurred with an initial batch of thunderstorms, an additional round of heavy rain in the early evening hours led to some renewed flooding from Frankfort to Herkimer.
ev: Video footage and trained spotter reported flash flooding along Mohawk Street and South Caroline Street in the Village of Herkimer resulting in some cars stranded in the flood waters.
State Route 5 between Ilion and Herkimer was closed due to flooding over various sections of the road.

Video and trained spotter reports were received of water and debris flowing down Steuben Hill Road in the Village of Herkimer with portions of the road getting washed out. The flood water and debris flowed onto some nearby side streets including Dayton Place.
Flooding was reported on New York Route 168 between Route 28 and Route 167 in the Village of Mohawk.
Photos were received of flash flooding at the intersection of East Main Street and State Route 5s in the Village of Mohawk.
Video was received of water rapidly flowing over Michigan Street and Marshall Avenue in the Village of Mohawk.
State Route 5s was closed from East Main Street in the Village of Mohawk to the South Washington Street Bridge in the Village of Herkimer due to flooding.
lsr: 9 cars reported stranded along Mohawk Street and South Caroline Street in Herkimer.
State Route 5 between Ilion and Herkimer reported closed due to flooding.
Report of Steuben Hill Road west of German Street partially washed out. Numerous additional streets in Herkimer including German Street near Lou Ambers Drive also flooded.
Flooding reported on New York Route 168 between Route 28 and Route 167 in Mohawk.
Photos received of flash flooding near the intersection of East Main Street and State Route 5s in the Town of Mohawk.
